record.paper_title: The Projection Technique for Two Open Problems of Unconstrained Optimization Problems
record.context_brief: BFGS global convergence under weak Wolfe-Powell search
record.original_question: For unconstrained optimization of a twice continuously differentiable nonconvex function f: R^n -> R, does the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno quasi-Newton method admit a globally convergent variant under the weak Wolfe-Powell line search? More specifically, can one obtain global convergence for nonconvex objectives in that weak Wolfe-Powell setting even though standard BFGS is known to fail in relevant counterexamples?

evidence.quote: the second is the global convergence of the Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno quasi-Newton method
The other is the global convergence of the BFGS method for nonconvex functions. It has been considered an open problem in unconstrained optimization

the given algorithms possess global convergence under the WWP line search and the normal conditions for nonconvex functions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: R^n -> R be twice continuously differentiable and bounded below, with gradient g = ∇f assumed to be Lipschitz continuous on the level set of the starting point. Consider the quasi-Newton iteration

  x_{k+1} = x_k + α_k d_k,   d_k = -B_k^{-1} g(x_k),

where {B_k} is updated by the Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (BFGS) formula

  B_{k+1} = B_k - (B_k s_k s_k^T B_k)/(s_k^T B_k s_k) + (y_k y_k^T)/(y_k^T s_k),

with s_k = x_{k+1} - x_k and y_k = g(x_{k+1}) - g(x_k), and where the step size α_k > 0 is chosen by the weak Wolfe–Powell (WWP) line search: there exist constants 0 < δ < σ < 1 such that

  f(x_k + α_k d_k) ≤ f(x_k) + δ α_k g(x_k)^T d_k,
  g(x_k + α_k d_k)^T d_k ≥ σ g(x_k)^T d_k.

It is known that for general nonconvex f the standard BFGS method under the WWP line search may fail to converge (counterexamples are known).

Question: Does there exist a variant of the BFGS quasi-Newton method (for instance, using a projection-type modification of the iterates and/or a modification of the WWP line search and/or the update formula) that, under standard regularity assumptions on f (twice continuous differentiability, lower boundedness, Lipschitz continuous gradient) but without assuming convexity, satisfies the global convergence property

  liminf_{k → ∞} ‖g(x_k)‖ = 0   (or, stronger, lim_{k → ∞} ‖g(x_k)‖ = 0)?
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works construct modified BFGS variants (using projection techniques and/or modified weak Wolfe–Powell line searches) that are globally convergent for nonconvex functions, thereby giving an affirmative answer in the "modified-variant" sense. However, the global convergence of the classical (unmodified) BFGS method with a standard Wolfe line search for general nonconvex functions remains an open problem, with known counterexamples (Dai; Mascarenhas) showing that standard BFGS can fail.

status_evidence.title: Global convergence of a family of modified BFGS methods under a modified weak-Wolfe–Powell line search for nonconvex functions
status_evidence.snippet: A new modified weak-Wolfe–Powell line search technique together with modified BFGS formulas yields global convergence for nonconvex functions.
status_evidence.claim: Modified BFGS variants under a modified WWP line search are globally convergent on nonconvex problems.

status_evidence.title: An adaptive projection BFGS method for nonconvex unconstrained optimization problems
status_evidence.snippet: An adaptive projection BFGS method is globally convergent for nonconvex problems under weak Wolfe–Powell conditions with a superlinear rate.
status_evidence.claim: A projection-based BFGS variant achieves global convergence for nonconvex objectives under WWP.

status_evidence.title: The global convergence of the BFGS method with a modified WWP line search for nonconvex functions
status_evidence.snippet: Global convergence of the classical BFGS method is established under a modified WWP line search for nonconvex functions.
status_evidence.claim: Classical BFGS attains global convergence under a suitably modified WWP line search.

status_evidence.title: The Projection Technique for Two Open Problems of Unconstrained Optimization Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Projection technique addresses two open problems including BFGS global convergence under WWP line search for nonconvex functions.
status_evidence.claim: A projection-modified BFGS algorithm is globally convergent under the WWP line search.
